RAINIER\_WEB\_SOLVE\_ID: problem102:69733bc585b79e78dc46711c433af303124a8183

We need determine the invariant factors of `J(\mathbb F_{5^{17}})`. Let `\pi` denote the Frobenius endomorphism of `J` over `\mathbb F_5`. The group is

```math
J(\mathbb F_{5^{17}})=\ker(\pi^{17}-1),
```

and its order is obtained from the characteristic polynomial of `\pi^{17}`.

### 1. Frobenius polynomial of `J`

The curve has genus `2`, so the Frobenius polynomial has the form

```math
P(T)=T^4+a_1T^3+a_2T^2+5a_1T+25.
```

Counting points on `C` over the first few extensions gives

```math
\#C(\mathbb F_5)=7,\qquad \#C(\mathbb F_{25})=51,\qquad \#C(\mathbb F_{125})=43,\qquad \#C(\mathbb F_{625})=91.
```

Using the standard Newton identities relating these point counts to the Frobenius traces gives

```math
a_1=1,\qquad a_2=13,
```

hence

```math
P(T)=T^4+T^3+13T^2+5T+25.
```

### 2. Frobenius over `\mathbb F_{5^{17}}`

Let the roots of `P(T)` be `\alpha_i`. The Frobenius polynomial over `\mathbb F_{5^{17}}` is

```math
P_{17}(T)=\prod_{i=1}^4(T-\alpha_i^{17}).
```

Using the Newton recurrences for the powers `\alpha_i^{17m}` gives

```math
\begin{aligned} P_{17}(T)= {}& T^4+841505101T^3\\ &+185344706963883313T^2\\ &+642017441558837890625T\\ &+582076609134674072265625 . \end{aligned}
```

Therefore

```math
|J(\mathbb F_{5^{17}})|=P_{17}(1),
```

which is

```math
|J(\mathbb F_{5^{17}})| = 582718811920940715544665.
```

Factoring,

```math
582718811920940715544665 = 3^2\cdot5\cdot103\cdot125721426520159809179 .
```

### 3. Determine the cyclic structure

For every prime `\ell\neq5` dividing the order, the number of cyclic `\ell`-primary factors is the multiplicity of `T-1` in `P_{17}(T)\pmod{\ell}`.

The relevant factorizations are:

For `\ell=3`,

```math
P_{17}(T)\equiv (T-1)(T+1)(T^2+T-1)\pmod3 ,
```

so `T-1` occurs once.

For `\ell=103`,

```math
P_{17}(T)\equiv (T-47)(T-1)(T+46)(T+47)\pmod{103},
```

again with a single `T-1`.

For

```math
\ell=125721426520159809179,
```

we get

```math
P_{17}(T)\equiv (T-a)(T-b)(T-1)(T-c)\pmod{\ell}
```

for distinct roots, so again the `T-1` factor has multiplicity one.

Thus each prime-to-`5` primary component is cyclic. The `3`-part has order `3^2`, the `103`-part has order `103`, and the large-prime part has order `125721426520159809179`.

The `5`-part has order only `5`, so it is necessarily cyclic as well.

Because all primary components are cyclic and their orders are pairwise coprime, their direct product is cyclic. Hence the whole Jacobian group is cyclic.

Therefore the invariant-factor decomposition is

```math
\boxed{ J(\mathbb F_{5^{17}}) \cong \mathbb Z/ 582718811920940715544665\mathbb Z }.
```

Equivalently,

```math
\boxed{ J(\mathbb F_{5^{17}}) \cong \mathbb Z/3^2\mathbb Z \times \mathbb Z/5\mathbb Z \times \mathbb Z/103\mathbb Z \times \mathbb Z/125721426520159809179\mathbb Z }
```

which combines into the single invariant factor above.
